# Skales

> Websites & systems for service businesses. Builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses (trades and local operators). Run by Tom Griffiths, one person, in the United Kingdom.

Key facts:
- Builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses (trades and local operators).
- One person: the person you message is the person who builds it.
- Thirty-six working demonstration builds run live on the site; every business in them is fictional.
- One system a week is built in public on Instagram.
- Clients own their domain, code and accounts from day one; nothing is rented back to them monthly.
- Every build is hand-coded with no page-builder, no theme and no third-party runtime dependencies.
- Contact: thomasrgriffiths08@gmail.com · Instagram @tomxsystems (https://www.instagram.com/tomxsystems/)
- Book a call: https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/book/

## Pages
- [Home](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/): what Skales builds, with a live demonstration build on the page.
- [Work — thirty-six builds](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/): every demonstration build, each running live and each with its own page.
- [Websites](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/websites/): the four kinds of website (loud, motion, quiet, direct) with every example.
- [Tools](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/tools/): the broad tools for any service business and the ones built for a single trade.
- [Services](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/): the five services, built as one system — [Websites](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/websites/), [Booking and CRM](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/booking-and-crm/), [Follow-up automation](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/follow-up-automation/), [Meta ads](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/meta-ads/), [Google ads](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/google-ads/).

## The thirty-six builds
- [Northgate Quote Engine](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/northgate-quote-engine/): business tool for an invented kitchen fitter — A quote that assembles itself while the customer answers.
- [Redgate Job & Lead System](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/redgate-job-system/): business tool for an invented heating & plumbing — Every enquiry, where it came from, and what happened to it.
- [Halcyon Dispatch](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/halcyon-dispatch/): business tool for an invented heating dispatch team — Drag a job to another engineer and the week re-plans itself.
- [Ledgerline](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/ledgerline/): business tool for an invented invoice & proposal studio — A live A4 page that reflows as you type.
- [Mortgage Lab](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/mortgage-lab/): business tool for an invented broker lead magnet — What an overpayment really saves, month by month.
- [Payslip Lab](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/payslip-lab/): business tool for an invented accountant lead magnet — Gross to net, and the 60% trap nobody explains.
- [Atelier Voss](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/atelier-voss/): website for an invented architecture practice — A studio site with no photographs at all.
- [Cadence](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/cadence/): website for an invented field-ops software — The page is an operations board that never stops running.
- [MARÉE — Sel Obscur](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/maree/): website for an invented fragrance house — Ink through water, and a page that darkens as you descend.
- [SIGNAL 2027](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/signal/): website for an invented music & light festival — Type that reacts to how hard you scroll.
- [Kerbside Scorecard](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/kerbside-scorecard/): business tool for an invented google profile report card — Marks a Google Business Profile like an exam.
- [Stopcock](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/stopcock/): business tool for an invented missed-call leak meter — What unanswered calls cost you a year.
- [Turnover](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/turnover/): business tool for an invented roofing firm rebuild — Drag the tape line across a 2011 site and its rebuild.
- [Fenwick Booking](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/fenwick-booking/): business tool for an invented heating engineer — Service, slot, deposit, confirmed — no phone tag.
- [Jobsheet](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/jobsheet/): business tool for an invented van-side job report — Fill it in from the van, the customer report writes itself.
- [Shiftbook](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/shiftbook/): business tool for an invented salon staff rota — Click a cell to place a shift. Clashes flag as you go.
- [Long Exposure](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/long-exposure/): website for an invented long exposure — A film company's site that plays like a film you can scrub.
- [Overhead](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/overhead/): website for an invented overhead — Scroll to climb — the valley draws itself in contours as you rise.
- [Southpaw](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/southpaw/): website for an invented boxing club, leeds — A boxing club site built as a fight card, run by a round timer.
- [Marrow & Pin](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/marrow-and-pin/): website for an invented tattoo studio, bristol — A flash wall that inks itself as you scroll past each sheet.
- [Hale & Partners](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/hale-and-partners/): website for an invented chartered accountants, harrogate — A year-end that settles, and the deadlines counted from today.
- [Fern Physio](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/fern-physio/): website for an invented fern physio — A drawn body with ten tappable points, and a booking flow behind it.
- [Kestrel Electrical](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/kestrel-electrical/): website for an invented two-van electrical firm — An electrician's page built as a fuse board — every job is a breaker.
- [Kerb & Camber](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/kerb-and-camber/): website for an invented kerb & camber mot centre — A UK number plate you type into, and the MOT date that comes back.
- [Ringsback](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/ringsback/): business tool for an invented heating firm, leeds — Missed-call text-back console: the text goes out, the reply lands here.
- [Starboard](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/starboard/): business tool for an invented shown running for aldercroft tree care — Asks for the review at the right moment, then helps you reply to it.
- [Slate](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/slate/): business tool for an invented ashgrove building & maintenance — Your own price book, and the estimate it builds in a minute.
- [Triage](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/triage/): business tool for an invented latchford locks & security — Every enquiry, every channel, sorted by who has waited longest.
- [Doorstep](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/doorstep/): business tool for an invented heating firm’s customer — The page the customer opens on their phone after they have booked.
- [Clockcard](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/clockcard/): business tool for an invented redgate works — Staff clock in from the van; the office watches the week fill up.
- [Boiler Book](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/boiler-book/): business tool for an invented ashgate heating — Thirty boilers sorted by what's due, with the chasing done for you.
- [MOT Minder](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/mot-minder/): business tool for an invented kilnbrook motors — Every car the garage has seen, and the texts that bring them back.
- [Chairside](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/chairside/): business tool for an invented four-chair salon — Rebooks the client at the counter and refills the slots that fall out.
- [Turntable](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/turntable/): business tool for an invented corncrake — The floor, the queue at the door and the deposit rule, on one screen.
- [Roofline](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/roofline/): business tool for an invented ackroyd roofing — A postcode and seven taps draw the roof, then price it.
- [Roundsheet](https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/work/roundsheet/): business tool for an invented nash window cleaning — The round in door order, with a DONE big enough for one thumb.

## Frequently asked
- **Do I actually own the website?** Yes. With Skales the domain, the code and the hosting sit in your own accounts from day one. It is set up so you could walk away tomorrow and lose nothing; that is the whole point.
- **Is there a monthly fee to keep my site online?** No. Skales does not charge a monthly platform fee to keep your own website alive. You pay for hosting and your domain directly, in your own name, at cost. If any quote you get includes a monthly fee to keep your own site online, that is rent.
- **How long does a build take?** A capture website takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks. You get a date with the quote, and you can watch it being built in public.
- **Are the thirty-six builds on this site real clients?** No, and deliberately so. Every business, person, review and phone number in the demonstration builds is invented, so nothing on this site exposes anyone Skales works with. They are real working software, just for businesses that do not exist.
- **Who actually does the work?** Tom Griffiths. Skales is one person: there is no account manager and no handover to a junior. The person you message is the person who builds it.
- **What kind of businesses is this for?** UK service businesses whose work comes in by phone: plumbers, heating engineers, electricians, roofers, kitchen fitters, landscapers, cleaners, salons and similar trades and local operators.
- **What happens after I book a call or send the form?** Tom Griffiths looks at your website, your Google listing and what happens when someone tries to reach you, then messages you three things: what is leaking, what to fix first, and what it is worth in jobs. If you want it fixed, you get a flat quote. If not, you keep the list.
- **Do you use page-builders or templates?** No. Every build is hand-coded with no page-builder, no theme and no third-party runtime dependencies. Every visual is drawn in code rather than bought from a stock library.

Quiet Plain, calm, expensive. Almost nothing moves; the typography does the work. 3 examples Accountants, clinics, architects, solicitors: businesses whose customers are buying reassurance. Direct Conversion first. One-tap call, a three-field form, the service area, no fluff. 3 examples Trades and local services that live off the phone. When does a business need a loud website? When being remembered matters more than being reassured. A boxing club or a tattoo studio is chosen on feel, so the site moves, the type hits and there is one thing the visitor will describe to a friend. Everything still works: the number, the booking and the address are one tap away. The story reads even if you never scroll. Because its customers are buying trust, not excitement. A quiet page uses real typography, generous space and one accent, and moves exactly once. The detail Straight answers What does a website for a service business need? Less than most have. A way to ring you in one tap, a short form for people who would rather type, the area you cover, proof that you are real, and a way to book if you take bookings. All of it has to work on a phone with one bar of signal, because that is where most of your customers find you. Everything else (sliders, stock photos of handshakes, a page about your mission) slows the page down and gets in the way of the call. Why hand-built rather than a page builder? A page builder rents you a template and charges you every month to keep it. A hand-built site has no builder, no theme and nothing loading in the background that you did not ask for, so it is fast, and it is yours. Nothing is rented back to you. You can see the difference in the builds on this site: every one is hand-coded, and every one runs. Will it help me get found on Google? It gives you the best chance. Each service you want to be found for gets its own page that answers what people actually search, with proper structured data, fast load times and your Google Business Profile linked and consistent. That is what Google and the AI assistants read. Nobody can promise the top spot, and anyone who does is guessing. ### Booking and CRM — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/services/booking-and-crm/

Online booking and CRM for service businesses | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Services / Booking and CRM Booking and a CRM that run the admin for you. Online booking lets customers take a free slot in your diary and pay a deposit to hold it, at any hour, without ringing you. The CRM puts every enquiry, quote and job on one board, and sends the confirmations, chasers and reminders on its own. Book a call Try the demo A missed call, booked in two minutes. A call rings out at 21:47. The system texts back, the customer books and pays a deposit, and the job lands on the board and in the diary. A made-up business, so the numbers are illustrative. Fictional business · illustrative numbers Play the film What you get Booking and CRM What is included? A booking page on your own website, showing only the slots you really have. Deposits taken at booking, for the jobs you choose. Confirmation and reminder texts sent automatically. One board for every enquiry, quote and job, wherever it came from. Quotes chased when they go quiet, on a schedule you set. Invoices and review requests sent when a job is marked done. Where every enquiry came from, so you know which channel books work. No app for your customers to download. It all works in their phone browser. The detail Straight answers How does online booking work? The customer picks the job they need, then a day and a time from the slots you actually have free. Slots that are taken are already gone, so double bookings cannot happen. Where your trade takes a deposit, they pay it by card on the same page. They get a confirmation straight away and a reminder before the day. You get the job in your diary with their details, their notes and the deposit marked paid. What does the CRM actually do? Every enquiry lands on one board, whether it came from your website, a missed call, Google or an ad: Enquiry, Quoted, Booked, Done. Moving a job along sends what should be sent at that stage: the reply, the quote, a chaser if it goes quiet, the confirmation, the reminder, the invoice and the review request. You stop running the business from your text messages, and nothing slips because you were busy. Why take a deposit? A booking with money behind it is a booking people keep. The deposit holds the slot, comes off the final bill, and means the time you have set aside is paid for. You choose which jobs take one and how much. Which searches will my ads show for? The ones that come from people ready to book: your trade, the job and your area, such as boiler repair near me or emergency electrician in your town. Missed call text back for UK businesses | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Automations / Missed-call text-back Missed-call text-back: every missed call gets a reply. Missed-call text-back sends a text to anyone whose call you could not answer, seconds after it rings out, with a link to book or a quick question. It turns a missed call into a conversation before they ring the next business on Google. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters Missed-call text-back Why does it matter? When you are up a ladder or under a sink, you cannot answer. Plenty of people who reach voicemail do not leave a message; they ring the next number instead. A text back in the first minute keeps them talking to you. How it works Step by step How does missed-call text-back work? The call rings out. You are on a job and cannot pick up. The call goes unanswered, as it would now. The text goes out. Seconds later, the caller gets a text from your business: sorry you missed them, here is a link to book, or reply and you will ring back. They book or reply. They pick a slot on your booking page, or reply with what they need. Either way they have stopped looking elsewhere. You see it all. The missed call, the text and what happened next sit on one card in your CRM, so you know who to ring and who has already booked. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Sorry I missed your call, I’m on a job. You can book a time here: larchfield.co.uk/book, or reply with what you need and I’ll ring you back. Larchfield Heating An example for Larchfield Heating, a made-up business. Yours is written with you, in your words. What it needs From you What does it need from me? A business number that can forward unanswered calls. Most UK mobile and landline networks can. Your booking link, if you take bookings. If not, the text asks what they need. The numbers you do not want texted, such as suppliers and family. See it run Live demos with a made-up business. You play the customer, then see what the business sees. About a minute each. Your phone forwards calls you do not answer, and the text goes out from there. You keep your number and answer calls exactly as you do now. Will it text suppliers, family or spam callers? Numbers you know can be left out, so only new callers get the text. How fast does the text go? Within seconds of the call ringing out, while the caller still has their phone in their hand. Will it spam my customers? No. It only texts people who have just rung you, once, about the call they made. Nobody is added to a marketing list. More in every question, answered . Automated Google review requests | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Automations / Review requests Review requests that go out while the job is fresh. A review request goes to the customer by text when the job is marked done, with one tap straight to your Google review box. Asking every customer at the right moment is how a small business builds its rating without chasing anyone. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters Review requests Why does it matter? Happy customers mean to leave a review and forget. The ones who remember unprompted are often the unhappy ones. Asking everyone, the same day, while they are still pleased with the work, changes who writes your reviews. How it works Step by step How does review requests work? The job is marked done. You move the job to Done in the CRM, or the invoice is paid. The request goes out. A couple of hours later, the customer gets a short text thanking them and asking for a review, with a link that opens your Google review box. One tap to review. They tap, pick the stars and write a line. No searching for your business, no signing in to anything new. You reply. New reviews show up for you to reply to, so every review gets a response in your name. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Thanks again for having us round today, Priya. No, and it should not. Google does not allow filtering out unhappy customers before asking for a review, so everyone gets asked. A business that does good work comes out of that well. When is the best time to ask? The same day, a couple of hours after the job, while the work is fresh and they are still pleased. The timing can be changed for your trade. Does it work for repeat customers? Yes. It can ask once and then leave them alone, so a regular is not asked after every visit. Can I show my reviews on my website? Yes. Service reminders text your customers when they are due again: the annual boiler service, the MOT, the next haircut, the gutter clean. The work that comes round every year gets booked without anyone having to remember to ring. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters Service reminders Why does it matter? Repeat work is the cheapest work you will ever win, and it is the easiest to lose. Customers do not forget you; they forget the date. Whoever reminds them first gets the job. How it works Step by step How does service reminders work? The job sets the date. Automatic quote follow-up for trades | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Automations / Quote chasing Quote chasing: no quote goes quiet without a follow-up. Quote chasing sends a friendly follow-up when a quote has not been accepted, a couple of days after it went out, with a link to accept or ask a question. Quotes that go quiet get a nudge without you having to remember who you priced up last Tuesday. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters Quote chasing Why does it matter? Pricing a job takes time, and most quotes are never chased because the person who wrote them is on another job. A customer who has gone quiet is often just busy. The one who follows up politely is the one they book. How it works Step by step How does quote chasing work? The quote goes out. You price the job and send it from the CRM. The customer gets a link to see it and accept it. The system watches. It knows whether they have opened it, and whether they have accepted. The chaser goes out. If the quote is still open after a couple of days, the customer gets a short, friendly follow-up with the link again. Accepted becomes booked. When they accept, the job moves to Booked and the confirmation goes out. If they say no, it is closed and you know. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Hi Priya, just checking the quote came through OK. Happy to answer any questions, or you can book a date here: larchfield.co.uk/q/4821 An example for Larchfield Heating, a made-up business. A booking deposit is a small payment the customer makes when they book online, which holds the slot and comes off the final bill. It turns a booking into a commitment, so the time you set aside is paid for. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters Booking deposits Why does it matter? A no-show costs you the job and the job you turned away to fit them in. A deposit is the simplest fix: a booking with money behind it is a booking people keep, and the ones who cannot make it let you know. How it works Step by step How does booking deposits work? They pick a slot. The customer chooses the job and a free time on your booking page. They pay the deposit. They pay by card on the same page. You choose which jobs take a deposit and how much. The slot is theirs. They get a confirmation with the deposit shown, and a reminder before the day. It comes off the bill. The deposit is taken off the final invoice. Your cancellation rules decide what happens if they cancel late. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? You’re booked: boiler service, Thursday 8 October at 8:00. On my way texts for trades and mobile services | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Automations / On-my-way texts On-my-way texts: the customer knows you are coming. An on-my-way text tells the customer you have set off, with a rough arrival time and who is coming, so they are in, the dog is shut away and the car is off the drive. One tap from the job sheet sends it. Book a call Try the demo Why it matters On-my-way texts Why does it matter? A wasted trip to an empty house costs a morning. A customer who is not sure when you are coming rings to ask, and calls you while you are driving. One text before you set off fixes both. How it works Step by step How does on-my-way texts work? You set off. On the way to the job, you tap On my way on the job sheet on your phone. The text goes out. The customer gets a text with who is coming and a rough arrival time. They get ready. They are in, the parking is clear, and they are not ringing you to ask where you are. Running late is one tap too. If a job overruns, one tap tells the next customer, so nobody is left waiting without knowing why. The message What the customer gets What does the text say? Hi Sam, Dan from Larchfield Heating is on his way and should be with you around 9:40. Reply if anything’s changed. An example for Larchfield Heating, a made-up business. A page builder is the right choice if you enjoy building, have the evenings to do it, and want a site online for a small monthly fee. A hand-built Skales site is the better choice when the website’s job is to bring in work: it is faster, it books and follows up on its own, and you own it outright. ### Every question, answered — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/faq/

Questions about websites, booking and ads | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / FAQ Every question, answered. Short, straight answers about what Skales builds, what it costs, how long it takes and who owns it, then the questions for each service, automation and comparison. If yours is not here, ask it on a call. The basics Websites Booking and CRM Follow-up automation Meta ads Google ads Missed-call text-back Review requests Service reminders Quote chasing Booking deposits On-my-way texts Skales vs a page builder Skales vs a monthly trade website Skales vs a missed-call app Skales vs a directory listing The basics Start here The basics What does Skales do? Skales builds websites, online booking and follow-up automation for UK service businesses, and runs Meta and Google ads that send people to them. The aim is one system that turns a search, a tap or a missed call into a booked job. Who is Skales for? Trades and local service businesses whose work comes in by phone, message or search: plumbers and heating engineers, electricians, roofers, builders, cleaners, garages, salons, clinics, and anyone else who books work with customers. Who will I actually deal with? Tom Griffiths. Skales is one person, so the person you message is the person who builds it. How much does it cost? Every job is quoted flat after a short call, and agreed before anything starts. The price depends on how many pages you need, whether you take bookings or deposits, which automations you want and whether you want ads. There are no prices on this site. How long does it take? A website on its own takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks, built in public so you can watch it being made. Do I own what you build? Yes. The domain, the code and the accounts are set up in your name from day one. Nothing is rented back to you monthly, and if you stopped working with me, everything would keep working. Can you guarantee I will rank first on Google? No, and nobody honest can. What a well-built site does is give you the best chance: pages written for what your customers search, proper structured data, a fast site and a consistent Google Business Profile. Searches for your trade in your area are the ones to win first. Are the businesses on this site real? No. Every business, person, review and phone number in the demos and builds on this site is invented, and each one is labelled. They show how the systems work; no client is named or shown. Can I try it before I talk to anyone? Yes. The live demos on the Try it page run in your browser: call a business, book a job, or move a lead across a CRM board, then see what the business sees. Websites The full page Websites How long does a website take? A website on its own takes days. A full system with booking and follow-up usually takes one to two weeks, and you can watch it being built. How much does a website cost? Every job is quoted flat after a short call, because the price depends on how many pages you need, whether you take bookings or deposits, and which automations you want. There are no prices on this site and no monthly fee for a page builder. Do I own the website? Yes. The domain, the code and the accounts are set up in your name from day one. If you stopped working with me tomorrow, the site would keep working. I already have a website. Will I lose my Google ranking if it is rebuilt? Not if it is done properly. Every old address is redirected to its new page, so the links Google already knows keep working, and the new pages are faster and better structured than the old ones. Booking and CRM The full page Booking and CRM Can customers book at night or at weekends? Yes, that is the point. The booking page shows your free slots at any hour, so a customer who finds you at 10pm books then, instead of meaning to ring you in the morning. Can two people book the same slot? No. A slot disappears the moment it is taken, on every device. Do my customers need to download an app? No. Booking, paying the deposit and every text they get works in the browser on their phone. I quote rather than book. Is this still for me? Yes. The CRM board works the same way for quotes: every enquiry gets a reply, every quote gets chased if it goes quiet, and accepted quotes become booked jobs. Can I see where my enquiries come from? Yes. Every enquiry is tagged with where it came from (your website, Google, a missed call, an ad), so you can see which ones turn into booked work. Follow-up automation The full page Follow-up automation What does it cost to run? The setup is quoted flat, like everything else. After that, each text costs a few pence from the text provider. Can I change what the messages say? Yes. Every message is written with you before it goes live, and any of them can be changed or paused with a message to me. Will it text my suppliers or family when I miss their calls? Not if you do not want it to. Numbers you know can be left out, so only new callers get the text. Do I need the website and CRM as well? No, but they work best together. Missed-call text-back and review requests can run on their own; quote chasing and reminders need somewhere to keep the jobs, which is what the CRM is for. Meta ads The full page Meta ads How much should I spend on ads? It depends on your area, your trade and how many jobs you can take on. We agree a test budget on the call, the spend goes to Meta from your own account, and you can change it at any time. Can you guarantee leads? No, and nobody honest can. What you do get is a clear view of what the ads cost and what they booked, so you can decide whether to keep going. Do I need a website first? The ads need a page built to book. If you do not have one, I build it as part of the job, and it carries on working for you whether the ads are running or not. Facebook or Instagram? Both run from one Meta account. Where the budget goes depends on where your customers are, and the tracking shows which one books. Who owns the ad account? You do. It is set up in your name like everything else, so if you stop working with me, the account, the audience data and the history stay with you. Google ads The full page Google ads How much should I spend on Google Ads? It depends on how competitive your trade is in your area and how many jobs you want. We agree a test budget on the call, the spend goes to Google from your own account, and you can change it at any time. How quickly do Google Ads work? Search ads can start showing as soon as Google approves them, so they are the fastest way to appear for searches you are not ranking for yet. Getting the cost per job down takes a few weeks of tuning. Should I do ads or SEO? Usually both. Ads bring enquiries while the website earns its place in the normal results, which takes months. Once the site ranks for a search, you can spend less on ads for it. Can you guarantee the top spot? No. Where an ad appears depends on the budget, the competition and Google. What you get is a clear view of what each booked job cost. Who owns the Google Ads account? You do. It is set up in your name, so the account, the data and the history stay with you. Missed-call text-back The full page Missed-call text-back Does it work with my mobile number? Yes. Your phone forwards calls you do not answer, and the text goes out from there. You keep your number and answer calls exactly as you do now. Will it text suppliers, family or spam callers? Numbers you know can be left out, so only new callers get the text. How fast does the text go? Within seconds of the call ringing out, while the caller still has their phone in their hand. Will it spam my customers? No. It only texts people who have just rung you, once, about the call they made. Nobody is added to a marketing list. Review requests The full page Review requests Can it only ask the happy customers? No, and it should not. Google does not allow filtering out unhappy customers before asking for a review, so everyone gets asked. A business that does good work comes out of that well. When is the best time to ask? The same day, a couple of hours after the job, while the work is fresh and they are still pleased. The timing can be changed for your trade. Does it work for repeat customers? Yes. It can ask once and then leave them alone, so a regular is not asked after every visit. Can I show my reviews on my website? Yes. Real reviews can appear on your site, and once there are enough, in your search results too. Nothing is ever made up. Service reminders The full page Service reminders Which businesses is this for? Any business where the work comes round: boiler services and landlord certificates, MOTs and car services, hair and beauty appointments, window and gutter cleaning, check-ups and maintenance contracts. Can it use my existing customer list? Yes. A spreadsheet with names, numbers and the date of their last job is enough to start. How many reminders does a customer get? Usually one, and one follow-up if they do not book. Then it stops until next time. Is it allowed to text past customers? A reminder about a service they have had before, from a business they used, is the kind of message most customers expect. Anyone who replies to opt out is never texted again. Quote chasing The full page Quote chasing Will customers find it pushy? Not one polite message a couple of days later. It reads like a business that cares about the job, and customers often reply to say they had simply not got round to it. How many times does it chase? Once by default, with a second follow-up if you want one. After that the quote is left alone. What if the customer has already accepted? Then no chaser goes. It only follows up quotes that are still open. Can I still send my own quotes? Yes. You price the job; the system sends it and follows it up. Booking deposits The full page Booking deposits Will a deposit put customers off? A small deposit on the booking page is normal for salons, clinics, restaurants and more and more trades. Customers who are serious about the job pay it; the ones who were never going to turn up tend not to book. Where does the money go? Straight to your own payment account, set up in your name. What if a customer cancels? Your rules decide. Many businesses refund with enough notice and keep the deposit for late cancellations, and the booking page says so before they pay. Can some jobs be booked without a deposit? Yes. You choose which jobs take one, so a free quote visit can be booked without paying anything. On-my-way texts The full page On-my-way texts Does it track my location? No. It sends the text when you tap the button, with the arrival time you choose. Nobody is followed on a map. Can my team use it? Yes. Each person taps from their own job sheet, and the text says who is coming. What about the night before? Every booking already gets a reminder the day before. The on-my-way text is for the morning of the job. Is this only for trades? No. It suits anyone who goes to the customer: cleaners, mobile hairdressers, dog groomers, mechanics, surveyors. If the domain is in your name, it moves with you. If the provider registered it in theirs, ask them to transfer it to you first. Skales vs a missed-call app The full page Skales vs a missed-call app Is missed-call text-back worth it on its own? Yes, a reply in the first minute is better than no reply. It is worth more when the text leads somewhere the customer can book. Can I keep my phone number? Yes. Your phone forwards the calls you do not answer, and you answer calls exactly as you do now. ### Plumbers and heating engineers — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/for/plumbers/

Websites for plumbers and heating engineers | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / By trade / Plumbers and heating engineers Built for the night the boiler gives up. A website for a heating engineer needs your Gas Safe number on every page, a call button that stays on screen, and separate pages for breakdowns, servicing, new boilers and landlord certificates, because that is how people search. It also has to catch the call you miss while you are under a boiler, and remind last year’s customers when their service is due. Book a call Try it as a heating engineer What it needs Plumbers and heating engineers What should a website for plumbers and heating engineers do? Your Gas Safe registration number on every page, with a link so customers can check it on the Gas Safe Register. A call button that stays on screen on a phone, for the person standing next to a cold radiator. Separate pages for breakdowns, annual servicing, new boilers and landlord gas safety certificates. Your customers How the work comes in How do customers choose a heating engineer? Nobody shops around for a boiler repair on a cold evening. A locksmith’s website has to prove two things fast to someone standing outside a locked door: that you are a real local locksmith rather than a call centre, and that they can reach you now. That means your name, face, van and area on the page, a call button that never leaves the screen, and a text back to any call you miss. Lockouts are searched for on a phone, on the doorstep, often in the dark, and the customer rings the first number that looks local. Many have heard of call centres that pass the job to whoever is free, so a real name, a real address and clear terms count for a lot. The rest of the work, lock changes after a burglary or a house move, upgrades for insurance and landlord changeovers, is planned and easily lost when the phone is the only way in. How it works → On-my-way texts Someone stuck outside wants to know who is coming and roughly when, and a text with your name is reassuring when a stranger is about to open their door. ### Own it. Don’t rent it. — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/why/

Why — one person, built in public, you own it | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Own it. Don t rent it. Skales exists because most service businesses are renting their own website from whoever built it, and getting a brochure for the money. This page is the reasoning, and the straight answers. Ownership Yours from day one Why should you own your own website? You should own your website because it is where your work comes from, and anything that important should not depend on a monthly payment to the person who built it. With Skales, the domain, the code and every account sit in the client s name from the first day. Some builders charge every month, forever, just to keep a site alive. A page-builder account the site cannot leave, a domain registered in the agency s name, a platform fee each one is a lever, and it only gets pulled one way. Every build here is hand-coded, hosted in an account the client controls, with the domain registered to the client. Sack Tom Griffiths tomorrow and everything keeps working. * If a quote includes a monthly platform fee to keep your own site online, that is rent. Walk away. One person No account manager Who builds it? Tom Griffiths does. Skales is one person, based in the United Kingdom, and the person you message is the person who does the work. There is no sales call handed to a junior, and nothing gets lost in a handover because there is not one. Operator Tom Griffiths. Builds every site and system personally. Base United Kingdom. Built for how UK service businesses get work: the phone, Google, word of mouth. Cadence One system a week, built in public on Instagram (@tomxsystems) . Method Hand-coded. No page-builders, no themes, no stock imagery, no third-party runtime. Proof Thirty-six working builds on the Work page , every one open to use. No. Skales does not charge a monthly platform fee to keep your own website alive. You pay for hosting and your domain directly, in your own name, at cost. If any quote you get includes a monthly fee to keep your own site online, that is rent. How long does a build take? A capture website takes days. ### What a missed call actually costs a service business — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/notes/what-a-missed-call-costs/

What a missed call actually costs a service business Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Notes 3 September 2026 Tom Griffiths What a missed call actually costs a service business The sum behind the missed-call text-back, with every assumption on the table — and why the number survives a sceptic. A missed call costs a service business more than the job on the other end of it, because the customer who rang is usually ringing the next firm on the list within the hour. The Stopcock calculator on this site meters that leak from five numbers you already know: calls per week, the share you miss, the value of an average job, how many quotes turn into work, and the share of missed callers who are gone for good. Why the model has a "gone for good" factor Most missed-call calculators quietly assume every missed caller would have booked. They would not. Some ring back, some were price-checking, some booked elsewhere before you saw the voicemail. Stopcock makes that share an explicit slider, so the headline figure is a floor a sceptical owner can defend, not a marketing number. What a text-back in under a minute changes A missed-call text-back sends the customer a message seconds after the ring-out, asks one question, and turns a voicemail into a conversation. The customer who was about to dial the next number replies instead. The follow-up automation on this site does exactly that, and the Redgate demo on the Why page shows the sequence end to end. Open the calculator, put your own numbers in, and argue with it. That is what it is for. Open the Stopcock calculator Book a call The work Book a call s k ales Websites systems for service businesses. One person, United Kingdom. ### Privacy notice — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/privacy/

Privacy notice | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Privacy notice Privacy notice Skales Studio is Tom Griffiths, one person in the United Kingdom. This page says what personal information the site and the studio collect, why, who else sees it, how long it is kept, and how to have it changed or deleted. Who is responsible for your information? Tom Griffiths, trading as Skales Studio, in the United Kingdom. For anything on this page, email thomasrgriffiths08@gmail.com . What is collected, and why? The 60-second check on /start. Your answers stay in your browser. If you choose to send your case file, it goes from your own phone, by WhatsApp, email or the share sheet, and I receive what you send. Booking a call. The booking page asks for your name, business, town, phone, email and what you would like help with. They are put into a message you send from your own WhatsApp or email, and I use them to prepare for the call. The free teardown. Your name, number and a line about your business, sent from your own WhatsApp or email. Messages. Whatever you send me by email, WhatsApp or Instagram, so I can reply. The live demos. Anything you type into the demos on /try/ stays in your browser and is not sent anywhere. Visiting the site. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, run by GitHub, which keeps standard server logs (IP address, browser and the pages requested) to keep it running and secure. The fonts load from Google Fonts, so Google receives your IP address when a page loads. Ads and analytics. None at the moment: the site runs no analytics or advertising tags. If that changes, a cookie banner will ask you first and this page will say so. Clients. If we work together: your contact and business details, the accounts and content the build needs, and invoices. On what basis? Replying to an enquiry you started and preparing a quote: steps you asked for before a contract, and my legitimate interest in answering. Doing the work: the contract. Keeping invoices and records: the law. Server logs: my legitimate interest in keeping the site working and secure. Who else sees it? Nobody buys it, and it is never sold or swapped. The services that handle it for me are the site’s host (GitHub), plus email and WhatsApp when you choose to use them, and anyone the law requires me to share it with. Does it leave the UK? Some of those services are run by companies based in the United States, including GitHub and Google. Where information goes outside the UK, it is covered by the safeguards UK data protection law requires, such as the UK–US data bridge or the contract clauses those companies use. How long is it kept? Enquiries that do not turn into work are deleted within 12 months of the last message. For clients, information is kept while we work together, and invoices and business records for as long as tax law requires. What can you ask for? You can ask to see what is held about you, have it corrected or deleted, restrict or object to how it is used, get a copy to take elsewhere. Email thomasrgriffiths08@gmail.com , and you will get an answer within one month. If you are unhappy with how your information has been handled, you can complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113. Last updated 8 October 2026. ### Cookies — https://thomasrgriffiths08-blip.github.io/skales/cookies/

Cookies | Skales Skip to content s k ales Work Try it Services About Book a call Work Try it Services About Free teardown Book a call Home / Cookies Cookies This site sets no advertising or analytics cookies. The little it stores is there because you are using it, like your place in a demo, and it stays in your browser. What does the site store without asking? Only what makes the pages you are using work. It stays in your browser and is not sent anywhere unless you choose to send it. What Where How long Why Your answers on /start and your place in the demos Session storage Until you close the tab So the check and the demos keep your answers as you move between screens. Where you arrived from, such as the Instagram link Session storage Until you close the tab So it can go with your case file, if you choose to send one. Are there ad or analytics cookies? No. The site runs no analytics or advertising tags at the moment. If that changes, a banner will ask you first, nothing will load unless you accept, and this page will list every cookie. How do you change your choice? There is nothing to change at the moment. You can clear this site’s data in your browser settings at any time. The privacy notice covers everything else.
